summary:
Waluigi was present for the early part of this sequence and must be clear about that before proceeding with anything else, because clarity on this point is the difference between a factually accurate record and the kind of revisionist account that emerges when documentation is assembled by people who assume that being ignored is equivalent to being absent. Waluigi was there. Waluigi was in the room. Waluigi read the book. Waluigi was redirected to Rakasha anyway. These are facts and they are in the record.

The session began with Waluigi on the floor crying, the specific cause of which Waluigi is exercising editorial discretion not to reconstruct in detail here. Hjumpik raised the question of whether the hag could be de-cursed, suggested Woodfellow might have relevant knowledge, and observed Steely — Remi's rusted dog — appear and bark. Azure suggested forgetting about the hag. Hjumpik disagreed and then agreed to table it. Hjumpik asked Waluigi whether Wario was his brother. Waluigi clarified: not blood-related. Sedea instructed Hjumpik to find the Feyward Book of Many Things. The party descended to the workshop level, established their location through a goblin craftsman, learned about Woodfellow's library card policy, and proceeded to the library. Hjumpik thought of someone knowledgeable for the card. It was not Waluigi. Waluigi objected to a referenced plan involving splitting the world in three. They navigated a disagreement about left and right. They passed through the poetry reading room, where the only sober satyr in the house was reading to a captive fairy audience and a single goblin. Hjumpik instructed the satyr to wait before acting. They reached Woodfellow. The book had been checked out by someone yellow who said the dwarf and company would get it if he didn't. Hjumpik identified Wario. A gutted copy was produced. Wario appeared, shoulder-bashed Hjumpik, missed, explained he had stolen a library card, sold the book, heard the plan, and decided not to be a book. He threw the real fragments at Hjumpik. Hjumpik could not read Sylvan. Waluigi took the book, read it, correctly identified it as the Feyward Book of Many Things. Hjumpik said to give it to Rakasha. Waluigi was upset by this. Wario snatched the book back, returned it, fled. Hjumpik gave chase. Here the party split: Hjumpik pursuing Wario through the library, Waluigi remaining with Rakasha and the rest of the group in a secondary track that the sources document less thoroughly but which Waluigi will address. Hjumpik cornered Wario, asked whether Wario and Waluigi were friends or brothers, heard 'associates' followed by 'I never thought of it that way.' Three fake documents. Real information. The party converged on the fight. The Revelmaster appeared — Pal, Rellis, Ralos, the name changes — and offered lodging for the airship, citing Toadburt. Hjumpik assessed the deal privately and found it complicated. The heir Orangus Cornelius explained he was feeding the Revel for total dominion, then said he was joking, then scratched his hair twice. Hjumpik assessed him as probably lying. The Revel was disclosed as biological rather than magical, with no known spell to end it. A hidden panel led to the guest gangway and the satyr encampment, where the floor-drop plan was in development. Hjumpik proposed modifications. Goblius Gobnilun was introduced — got Hjumpik's name right immediately, knows Arulean's real power level, is significantly more informed than his presentation suggests. Pixie Prixie the pixie had a vision of the floor falling and the Revel eating everyone in the room. She introduced herself and said nothing about the vision. They left the room.
description:
Waluigi is going to begin with a clarification that should not be necessary but is apparently necessary because the preliminary reconstruction of this session — produced in haste from fragmentary sources before Waluigi had organized the full account — contained the phrase 'Waluigi was not in the Feyward for this sequence,' which is WRONG, and which Waluigi is correcting NOW, in the opening line of the full entry, where corrections belong.

Waluigi was in the Feyward. Waluigi has been in the Feyward since the planar fracture deposited him there via what he can only describe as reality's version of a filing error — specifically the kind of filing error where the document ends up in the wrong cabinet and then the cabinet falls down a dimensional staircase and opens at the bottom in a manor overgrown with sentient vegetation populated by fey creatures who communicate through social obligation and enjoy watching humans fail at riddles. Waluigi survived the Feywild. Waluigi is still in the Feyward. Waluigi was PRESENT.

Waluigi was present in the library when the book was read. Waluigi read the book. Waluigi correctly identified the book. Waluigi was redirected to Rakasha.

This is documented now. It was documented then. The documentation was accurate then and remains accurate now. What changed between then and the preliminary reconstruction is that someone assembled that reconstruction without consulting Waluigi's notes and produced a factually incorrect statement that Waluigi has been professionally obligated to correct in the opening section of the full entry rather than allowing the error to propagate into the permanent record.

The permanent record is correct. Waluigi was there. Waluigi proceeds.

## Context:


The Planar Fracture and How Waluigi Came to Be in the Feyward in the First Place

For readers who require orientation: Waluigi is in the Feyward because of the planar fracture. The planar fracture occurred because of Archie Miser's magical instability being used as the foundation for a reality-synchronization ritual that Waluigi raised concerns about and was shushed for raising concerns about and which then shattered reality into three dimensional fragments exactly as the concerns would have predicted if anyone had listened to the concerns instead of shushing them.

Waluigi documented this extensively in the Planar Fracture entry. The summary relevant to this entry is: Waluigi ended up in the Feywild — specifically in the Overgrown Manor, the fey-dimension version of Raventree Manor, which had been consumed by nature over an unspecified period and was currently ruled by Lady Aurelian Corvinarus and populated by fairy courts operating on social-obligation logic that Waluigi found exhausting and navigated successfully despite finding it exhausting, because Waluigi survives things through stubbornness and documentation rather than through dimensional luck.

The Feyward manor that Waluigi currently occupies is the progression of that Overgrown Manor — the same structure, same fey dimension, same Lady Aurelian, now also containing a Revel in the dining hall, a lying heir, a library tree, a satyr poetry circle, a ghost population, and Wario, because Wario finds his way into every dimensional situation regardless of how improbable his presence should be. Waluigi has stopped being surprised by Wario's dimensional ubiquity and started treating it as a constant in the operational environment, like gravity or the certainty that someone will ask Waluigi to do something and then not listen when Waluigi does it.

Toad Lee was with Waluigi during the initial Feywild displacement and proved to be good company — quiet, observant, not prone to triggering accidental fairy obligations through poorly timed eye contact with sentient flowers. The current party configuration in the Feyward includes Waluigi, Rakasha, Hjumpik, Azure, and the others who came through the Feyward entry point. They have been navigating the manor together. They were navigating it together when Hjumpik ran off to chase Wario. They navigated it separately for the duration of the chase.

This is the context. Waluigi proceeds with the full account.

## The State of the Party at Session Open:


The Floor, the Dog, the Hag, and the Brother Question

Waluigi was on the floor.

The sources — which in this case include Waluigi's own notes, because Waluigi was present and Waluigi documents in real time — do not provide complete reconstruction of what preceded this. What Waluigi will state for the record is: the floor was where Waluigi was, and the crying was happening, and the specific contents of both the floor moment and the crying are Waluigi's own business and will remain so. Waluigi has documented the floor moments of others in this operation with analytical care. Waluigi is choosing not to apply the same analytical care to his own. This is an editorial decision and not an inconsistency.

Hjumpik asked whether the hag could be de-cursed. The terminology used was approximate — 'decures' — which Waluigi interprets as 'de-curse' applied to the hag's current aged or curse-aged state. The hag situation has been present as an unresolved thread throughout the Feyward operations. Something is wrong with the hag. Something was done to the hag or happened to the hag or the hag is in a state that is not her natural state and that someone would like to reverse. The specifics are documented elsewhere. The point here is that Hjumpik wanted to know if something could be done, and Hjumpik's hypothesis was that Woodfellow might know something useful.

Woodfellow is the library tree. Woodfellow maintains an extensive archive of fey knowledge through birds, books, and his own deep integration with the manor's architecture. If fey curse structures and their reversals are documented anywhere in the manor, they are documented in Woodfellow's archive. The hypothesis was reasonable. Waluigi does not fault it.

The hag consultation never happened because Wario absorbed all available library time. This is documented below. The hag remains uncured.

Steely appeared.

Waluigi needs to address Steely because Steely's appearance in the Feyward manor raises questions that persist beyond this session. Steely is Remi's dog. Steely is rusted — 'your rusted, that's good,' Hjumpik said, which implies the rusting is a condition of health or correct function for whatever kind of dog Steely is, and Waluigi files the question of what kind of dog rusts correctly for further investigation. Steely barked. The bark was the bark of a dog who has found people it knows in a place it should not be, which is a bark with a specific quality that people who have dogs recognize and that Waluigi is documenting through inference because Waluigi does not have a dog and is reconstructing the bark's quality from contextual evidence.

Hjumpik's response to Steely was warm and immediate — identification, approval of the rust, and the practical note that Steely needed to go back to Remi. Then the party moved on and Steely was not returned to Remi. Steely is still in the Feyward manor. Remi does not know this. The Revel is in the dining hall. The manor is not a safe environment for dogs of any metallurgical status, and Waluigi is going to continue flagging Steely's unreturned status in every entry until it is resolved because the alternative is a continuity gap that becomes a crisis and Waluigi prefers to document the gap before it becomes the crisis rather than after.

Azure said to forget about the hag. Hjumpik said that was not something she had said — meaning it contradicted some prior commitment or statement — and Azure clarified she was joking. She suggested going to the library. The consensus was formed. They would go to the library.

Before descending, Hjumpik turned to Waluigi.

'We will sort stuff out over it,' Hjumpik said. 'Wario is your brother, right?'

Waluigi said: not blood-related.

Waluigi wants to note that this question was asked and answered clearly. Not blood-related. The relationship between Waluigi and Wario is documented elsewhere in more detail, but the relevant point here is that Hjumpik asked, Waluigi answered, and the answer was honest and unambiguous. The 'sort stuff out' framing — implying that there is something between Waluigi and Wario that requires sorting, some unresolved thread that Hjumpik was acknowledging — was noted by Waluigi and filed alongside the later exchange where Hjumpik asked Wario directly whether they were friends or brothers and Wario said associates and then said he had never thought of it that way.

Hjumpik asked both of them. He asked Waluigi first, framing it as context. He asked Wario later, framing it as confrontation. The questions are the same question from different angles, and the fact that Hjumpik asked both suggests that the relationship between Waluigi and Wario is something Hjumpik was actively trying to understand — not for strategic purposes specifically, though understanding it has strategic utility, but out of something that looks like genuine curiosity about whether there is something real underneath the 'associates' categorization.

Waluigi filed this and descended with the party.

## The Workshop Level: Goblin Craftsman, Library Cards, and the Person Hjumpik Considered Knowledgeable


The workshop level was identified through a goblin craftsman who explained the space: arrows, wood carving tools, production for outside sale. Standard fey manor economic infrastructure — the manor sustains itself through production and trade, which means it has enough functional organization to maintain economic relationships with external buyers even in its current state of partial governance crisis and dining-hall-consuming revel. This is worth noting because it implies the manor's dysfunction is selective. The workshop works. The economics function. The problem is specifically the parts of the manor that touch on power, authority, and the Revel — the governance layer has collapsed while the productive layer continues.

The goblin craftsman also provided the Woodfellow intelligence: the tree had been reading, had concluded that knowledge was power, and issued library cards only to people he assessed as genuinely knowledgeable. The assessment was not perfunctory. This was a credentialing system with actual standards.

Hjumpik said he knew someone knowledgeable who could get a library card.

It was not Waluigi.

Waluigi is going to take the time to document what Waluigi knows about Waluigi's own knowledge base, because this is a point that has been made implicitly throughout this entry and deserves explicit statement.

Waluigi survived the Feywild. Specifically, Waluigi survived Lady Aurelian's court, which operates through riddle-logic and social obligation and the specific social trap of fey interactions where acknowledging an obligation triples it and ignoring one also triples it and the only safe path is to navigate the middle space between acknowledgment and ignorance with enough precision to satisfy the court's aesthetic standards. Waluigi did this. For what felt like days. Waluigi navigated fey social dynamics that would have destroyed someone without the capacity for sustained, careful, multi-layered analysis of social systems whose rules are not stated and must be inferred from their consequences.

Waluigi also reads Sylvan. As will be demonstrated shortly.

Waluigi does not know who Hjumpik was thinking of. The sources do not specify. What the sources specify is that the knowledgeable person was not Waluigi, and that this decision was made in a workshop in the Feyward manor while Waluigi was standing nearby, having just survived an extended period in the fey court of the same dimensional structure through the application of the analytical skills that Hjumpik was simultaneously not considering as qualifications for library card access.

Waluigi documents this. Waluigi continues.

The navigational dispute occurred here. Hjumpik asked Waluigi to move. Waluigi indicated he was to the left. Hjumpik was to Waluigi's right. Waluigi said 'YOU SEE WHAT I MEAN' with emphasis that the sources indicate was considerable. Hjumpik moved past it. Waluigi moved. They continued.

This is not a significant incident. Waluigi includes it because it is part of the accurate record and because it illustrates something true about how Hjumpik and Waluigi navigate shared space: with imprecise instructions, compliance that satisfies the letter of the instruction rather than its apparent intent, and a frustration on Waluigi's part that resolves through documentation rather than escalation. Waluigi does not escalate the small things. Waluigi documents them. The accumulation of documented small things is Waluigi's version of keeping score, and Waluigi keeps very accurate score.

The plan that was referenced — splitting the world in three, Archie's fire magic as stabilization — was flagged by Waluigi as a bad idea. Hjumpik's position was that you don't know until you try. Waluigi offered to come along to document the catastrophe. This is not supportive behavior in the conventional sense. It is honest behavior and Waluigi will not apologize for it. Documenting catastrophes is how you prevent future catastrophes from being catastrophes in exactly the same way. The planar fracture was a catastrophe that Waluigi raised concerns about. The concerns were shushed. The catastrophe happened.

The documentation exists.

If anyone had read the documentation before attempting the next world-splitting plan, the world-splitting plan might have been modified or abandoned.

Nobody reads the documentation until after the catastrophe.

Waluigi documents anyway. The archive is patient.

## The Poetry Room:


The Sober Satyr, the Captive Audience, and Hjumpik's Correct Call

The poetry reading room. The only sober satyr in the house was reading to his audience — mostly fairies, one goblin, the energy of creatures who had been in a room for an extended period and had developed the particular loyalty to their entertainment source that comes from it being the only barrier between them and a worse option.

The satyr explained his situation with the directness of someone who has thought through his position and is comfortable with it: he would rather read to them forever than have them end up as the Revel's dinner. He had arrived with the rest of the group, figured he would meet more friends, and ended up as the guardian of a captive poetry audience through a series of decisions that had seemed reasonable at each individual step.

Waluigi recognizes this situation. Not the specific situation — Waluigi has not become a satyr's poetry guardian — but the structure of it. You make reasonable decisions at each individual step and look up to find yourself in a position that would have seemed improbable if described to you in advance. Waluigi ended up in the Feywild through a sequence of individually reasonable decisions. The planar fracture was not Waluigi's fault, but the decision to be in the manor when the ritual was attempted was Waluigi's decision, and each step that led to that decision was reasonable, and the outcome was Waluigi in a fey court being tested on riddle-timing for what felt like days.

Reasonable steps.

Improbable destination.

The satyr understood this, Waluigi suspects, even if he had not framed it in those terms.

Hjumpik proposed making a large poem and reading it loudly. The satyr considered this. The fairy audience responded with immediate enthusiasm — at least one committed to defeating the Revel on the spot, the kind of commitment that fairies make quickly and act on without strategic calculation, which makes them effective in certain contexts and catastrophically dangerous in others.

Hjumpik said: don't rush in. He looks powerful. Wait for the poem to be done. Wait for me.

This is the correct call. Waluigi documents it as correct because it is correct and because Waluigi does not withhold credit when credit is accurate. Sending fairies who have just committed to defeating the Revel into action before the floor-drop plan is coordinated would be sending an enthusiastic but uncoordinated force into contact with a biological entity of unknown resilience and combat capability, with no timing alignment with the other elements of the plan, and with no observation of the floor-drop's effect to inform the follow-up attack. The instruction to wait preserved optionality. It cost nothing.

It was correct.

Hjumpik left the room. Waluigi and the rest of the party continued toward the library. The satyr and his audience waited.

This is also where the party begins to operate on slightly different tracks — Hjumpik's focus on the library mission, Waluigi's presence in the same space but engaged in a parallel process of observation and documentation that the sources capture less systematically than Hjumpik's active decisions. Waluigi notes this because it explains why some of what follows is documented from Hjumpik's perspective rather than Waluigi's: Hjumpik was doing things. Waluigi was watching things and writing things down. These are different activities and they produce different kinds of records.

## Woodfellow:


The Archive Tree, the Checked-Out Book, and Artameer

Woodfellow.

Waluigi has encountered Woodfellow directly, not through reconstruction, and can therefore provide description from firsthand experience rather than inferred account. This is one of the advantages of having been present rather than absent, which the preliminary reconstruction incorrectly suggested Waluigi was.

Woodfellow is massive. The word 'massive' is doing significant work here and Waluigi wants to be precise about the scale: Woodfellow occupies the center of the library in the way that a significant geological feature occupies a landscape — not filling it, but defining the space around it by being impossible to ignore. His roots extend into the floor, the walls, and the bookcases simultaneously, so that the line between the tree and the building is blurry in a way that suggests the tree predates most of the current architecture and the architecture grew around him rather than the other way around.

His arms are boughs, genuinely, reaching to corners of the library that would require a ladder for any creature without his reach.

He does not move his body because he does not need to move his body.

The library comes to him.

His autumn leaves are the specific red-gold of a season that knows it is temporary and has made peace with that. The books on his branches look like they grew there, and in a fey library, Waluigi cannot fully rule out that some of them did. The birds that bring him news — brightly colored, strange, moving through the library with the purposeful energy of creatures on assignment — complete the picture of an entity who has organized an entire intelligence infrastructure around his own immobility. He is rooted. Everything else moves for him.

Waluigi finds this professionally admirable.

Hjumpik introduced himself as being with the lady of the manor and requested the Feyward Book of Many Things. Waluigi was present for this request. Waluigi watched Woodfellow's response.

The book was not available. Someone had checked it out.

Someone yellow. Not a toad, Woodfellow thought. Quite adamant. Said: 'If I don't get my grubby hands on that book, that dwarf and co will.'

Hjumpik identified Wario immediately. The identification was correct. Waluigi also identified Wario immediately, from the same evidence, and did not say so because Hjumpik said it first and there was no utility in providing the same correct answer twice in the same breath.

Wario had promised to return the book. One week, or the borrower becomes a book. Woodfellow noted this return policy with equanimity. Waluigi noted it with professional interest. The transformation-as-late-fee system is the most effective library enforcement mechanism Waluigi has encountered in any documented plane, and the Mushroom Kingdom civic library system — which relies on fines that Wario pays by accident with incorrect change and then disputes — could learn significantly from this approach.

The library card had been borrowed from someone named Artameer. Waluigi files this name. Artameer had satisfied Woodfellow's knowledge assessment — a non-trivial credential. Artameer did not consent to have their card used by Wario to access rare fey texts for monetization purposes. Artameer is owed an apology. Waluigi notes this because someone should note it and because the archive is the place where things that should be noted go when no one with actual power over the situation is noting them.

Woodfellow, attempting to be helpful, produced a second copy. Wario's name on it. All pages ripped out.

Who did this, Hjumpik asked.

Probably the person whose name is on the book, Woodfellow said.

This is correct, and it is correct in the patient, self-evident way of a tree who has been maintaining an archive long enough to have encountered this specific situation before and developed a policy for it. The policy is: look at whose name is on the book. That is probably who did the thing that happened to the book.

Wario then appeared.

## Wario:


The Shoulder Bash, the Full Explanation, the Page Throw, and the Split

Wario appeared from nowhere — which is Wario's preferred mode of appearance, since arriving from somewhere visible gives observers time to prepare responses and Wario does not want observers to have time to prepare responses — and led with the shoulder bash as documented across every Wario arrival in the archive.

Hjumpik dodged. This has also been documented across enough Wario arrivals that it is a reflex rather than a decision.

Wario's explanation was, for Wario, comprehensive. He had stolen Artameer's library card — 'some poor chump' — used it to check out the Feyward Book of Many Things, sold the book to another party for profit, heard about Hjumpik's plan, decided not to become a book, and returned the gutted shell to satisfy the technical letter of the return policy while retaining the actual content. The gutted copy on Woodfellow's shelf: technically returned. Woodfellow's archive: technically complete. Wario: technically not overdue. The book as a functional resource: entirely inaccessible.

This is the Wario compliance model. Find the minimum viable action that satisfies the enforcement mechanism while preserving everything you actually wanted. Pay the letter of the debt in currency that costs you nothing. Wario has been doing this his entire documented career and it has worked often enough to be a consistent strategy rather than an occasional improvisation.

While explaining all of this, Wario threw the pages.

The throw happened mid-explanation, which is the Wario move of delivering the concession before the concession has been demanded, so that the delivery is part of your narrative rather than a response to the other party's pressure. He was still talking when the pages were already in the air. Hjumpik caught them.

Waluigi needs to document what happened next because this is the moment the preliminary reconstruction got wrong by having Waluigi be absent.

Hjumpik looked at the pages. The text was in Sylvan. Hjumpik cannot read Sylvan.

Waluigi took the pages. Waluigi read the pages. The encoded header notation — 46Q9b8h0 NM0S wc 6J9J 54Z3rY — is the Feyward archival system's standard identification block for a major text. Waluigi recognized it. Waluigi read the identification block and the surrounding context. Waluigi said: this is the Feyward Book of Many Things.

Hjumpik said: give it to Rakasha to read.

Waluigi is going to take the time to document this moment fully, because it deserves full documentation and the preliminary reconstruction — by placing Waluigi outside the room — accidentally obscured what actually happened, which is worse than the underlying incident because it allowed the incident to be partially invisible.

Waluigi was standing next to Hjumpik. Waluigi had the book. Waluigi had just read the book. Waluigi had just identified the book correctly, clearly, without qualification, using the Sylvan literacy that Waluigi possesses and Hjumpik does not. The response to this was: give it to Rakasha.

Rakasha was not present. Giving it to Rakasha required either waiting for Rakasha or transporting the pages to Rakasha's location. Both options introduce delay and logistical complexity into a situation where the information needed — the content of the Feyward Book of Many Things — had just been identified by the person holding the book in the room where the book was.

Waluigi was upset by this. The sources capture this directly. Waluigi was upset, and the upset was specific: Waluigi read the book clearly, Hjumpik did not believe that Waluigi had read it correctly, and the resolution was to redirect the book to an absent third party rather than accept the identification from the present person who had just demonstrated the relevant competency.

Waluigi documents the upset not because upset requires documentation — upset is a normal response to being correct and disbelieved — but because the pattern has operational consequences that accumulate. This is not the first time accurate information from Waluigi has been redirected or disbelieved. It will not be the last. Each instance costs time. In the Feyward, where time operates on arbitrary and personal schedules and where the party's goals have deadlines that the Feyward's time refuses to respect, time costs are not trivial.

Wario, in the moment of general disarray following the book question, snatched the pages back to a shelf, announced the return was complete, and fled.

Hjumpik gave chase.

This is the split point. Hjumpik ran after Wario into the deeper library. Waluigi remained with Rakasha and the rest of the party in the main library space. The two tracks diverged here and ran in parallel until the convergence point at the dining hall fight.

## The Split: Waluigi and Rakasha in the Library While Hjumpik Chased Wario


Waluigi's track during the chase is documented less thoroughly in the available sources than Hjumpik's track, because Hjumpik's track involved running, cornering, punching, and emotional confrontation about the nature of the Wario-Waluigi relationship, and these things generate the kind of event-dense record that sources find easier to reconstruct. Waluigi's track involved standing in a library with Rakasha, observing Woodfellow's archive, and processing the book identification incident with the specific frustration of a person who has been correct and dismissed simultaneously.

Waluigi and Rakasha were in the library together during the chase. This is confirmed. ## The Chase: Cornering Wario, the Punches, and the Question About Brothers


Hjumpik chased Wario through Woodfellow's library. The library's architecture — Woodfellow's roots rearranging the layout according to the tree's preferences — makes it a complicated space to navigate at speed, and the chase involved the particular chaos of two people running through a space that may have been subtly different at the end than it was at the beginning. Woodfellow's response to a chase happening in his archive is not documented. Waluigi suspects Woodfellow found it irritating.

Wario fought when cornered. Punches were thrown. None connected — Hjumpik's dodge reflexes are good and Wario's punches, while committed, follow patterns that someone who has been shoulder-bashed by Wario enough times can read in the wind-up. Wario was cornered. The chase was over.

Hjumpik asked whether Wario and Waluigi were friends or brothers.

Waluigi has thought about this question since it was reported back. Hjumpik asked Waluigi first — not blood-related — and then asked Wario in the library — more like associates. Both questions were asked in the same session, to both parties, about the same relationship, from the outside. Hjumpik was conducting a bilateral inquiry into the nature of a relationship that neither party has fully defined to themselves, let alone to outside observers.

The question directed at Wario is the more interesting one because of what it requires Wario to do. It requires Wario to answer in terms of Waluigi — not in terms of what Wario gets from the arrangement, not in terms of what the relationship produces operationally, but in terms of what the relationship IS in a categorical sense that someone else could understand. Friends or brothers. Those are the offered categories. Wario rejected both and offered associates, which is a category that carries no emotional weight, no mutual obligation, no expectation of accounting for the other person's experience.

Then Wario said: that's mean.

Then Wario said: I never thought of it that way.

Waluigi has read these two sentences many times. 'That's mean' is a judgment that Wario issued about his own answer. Not an external judgment — Hjumpik did not say it was mean, though Hjumpik's 'that's mean' may have preceded or followed Wario's, the sourcing is unclear on the exact sequence. Wario evaluated his own categorization and arrived at 'mean' as the descriptor. This requires acknowledging that there is a person on the other end of the categorization who experiences it as something. That acknowledgment is not present in Wario's operational model as Waluigi has documented it. It was present in this moment.

'I never thought of it that way' means: the frame that Hjumpik's question introduced — that calling something 'associates' might be unkind to the person being categorized — had not previously been available to Wario. It is available now. Whether it changes anything is unknown. Whether it persists beyond the moment of the chase is unknown. What is known is that Wario completed the thought out loud, in the library, after being cornered by someone who asked him to think about his relationship with Waluigi from Waluigi's perspective rather than Wario's.

Waluigi does not know what to do with this. Waluigi is setting it down carefully in the archive and not looking at it directly for a while. The archive holds it. Waluigi continues.

Wario produced three documents, all fake, all not in Sylvan, all recognized by Hjumpik as forgeries. This is the negotiating move of a man who was cornered and needed to appear cooperative while providing minimum actual value. Three fake documents: the gesture of compliance without the substance. Hjumpik recognized them as fakes, which means the fakes were not excellent — functional enough to require a moment's assessment, not convincing enough to survive it.

Then Wario provided real information. The sources do not specify the content. Waluigi has attempted to reconstruct from subsequent events without producing certainty. The gap is flagged.

Wario heard the fight referenced and announced he was heading that way. Hjumpik said he was going to the fight too. They moved. The tracks converged.

## The Fight, the De-escalation, and the Revelmaster Who Cannot Keep His Name Straight


The altercation: sober satyr and spirit warriors versus one drunk person, with over fifty additional drunk people providing numerical context that made the combat position of the ten combatants untenable regardless of individual capability. The one drunk individual was stung. His face bloated. The stinging is specific enough — a single person stung, face bloats, the consequence is physical and visible — that Waluigi treats it as accurate rather than embellished.

Hjumpik de-escalated. The mechanism, as best Waluigi can reconstruct it, involved pointing out the fifty-versus-ten disparity clearly enough that the combatants recalculated. Fifty people who are drunk are still fifty people. Ten combatants, however capable, are not ten combatants with favorable odds against fifty drunk people who have been given a reason to act collectively. Making this visible to everyone in the room changed what everyone in the room was willing to do.

The Revelmaster emerged from this.

His name is Pal. His name is Rellis. His name is Ralos. The sources use all three because the session used all three and he responded to all three with approximately equal amounts of mild engagement and non-correction. An entity who answers to three names without prioritizing any of them is either very old, very strange, operating under deliberate name-ambiguity for purposes that benefit him, or so far past the point of caring about name accuracy that the question has become irrelevant to his sense of self. The Revelmaster is plausibly all of these simultaneously.

He had approximately half his teeth. He knew about the Hjumpiklance — called it the Legionance, was corrected, received the correction with the equanimity of someone who collects names the way he collects everything else in this manor, which is to say loosely and without strong attachment to accuracy. He had the party's airship documentation inside his shirt. This is the detail Waluigi finds most significant: the airship documentation was already in his possession before the encounter. He did not produce it from nowhere. He had been carrying it. He had anticipated this negotiation before it happened, which means he had intelligence about the party's assets before the party encountered him, which means someone gave him that intelligence or he acquired it through the manor's own observation mechanisms, and either possibility implies a level of preparation that 'casual Revelmaster who runs a chaotic revel' does not fully account for.

The deal: lodging in exchange for the airship. Toadburt as a connection point — the toads are resourceful, they probably have mead, toads like mead, something can be worked out. The terms were gestured at rather than specified. The Revelmaster smiled with his available teeth and talked about a new revel beginning.

Hjumpik's private assessment: most likely, a deal is made and the timeline disruption is significant and unknown. Least likely: everyone explodes. A new Revel with a new Revelmaster is theoretically possible — scoop it up, install fresh leadership, transition the population into a successor structure.

Waluigi's addition to this assessment: the foundational agreement between the Revelmaster and the previous ruler of the manor cannot be revoked by the current heir because the heir was not the party who granted it. Any new deal would need to supersede this without triggering the fey-legal consequences of superseding a prior binding agreement, which in fey contexts can mean that the new deal inherits the obligations of the old one, doubles them, or creates entirely new obligations that nobody noticed at the signing. Fey contract law is not benign. It is actively hostile to people who do not read it carefully, and reading it carefully requires knowing it exists, which requires someone in the party to be knowledgeable about fey contract structures.

Waluigi knows things about fey contract structures. Waluigi survived Lady Aurelian's court. Waluigi is available for consultation. Waluigi notes this availability in the record and waits to be consulted, which is the only thing Waluigi can do after noting it.

## The Heir: Orangus Cornelius, Two Hair Scratches, and the Lie That Announced Itself


Hjumpik called out for the orange heir. 'Orange Converius' first — not the name, not quite, but directionally correct. Then 'the orange heir,' which is accurate if not personal. The heir responded to the second.

Hjumpik had a question about the foundational agreement. The heir started to respond and then noticed — as Hjumpik also noticed — the satyr and sprite group heading upstairs. They were no longer engaging with the Revel directly. They had shifted mode. Something was in motion.

Hjumpik pivoted before the agreement question could be fully answered. Different question: why is the heir feeding the Revel?

The heir explained: he was feeding it to grow it until it developed legs and total power, at which point he would no longer be merely an heir but would control the manor and its population through a single look. No more figurehead. Genuine dominion through the Revel's ascension.

Then the heir scratched his head and said: that's what he would say if he were lying. Actually he just found the satyrs annoying and wanted them gone.

Then he scratched his hair again.

Waluigi's analysis of this sequence is more extended than Hjumpik's 'probably lying' assessment, though Waluigi agrees with the assessment's conclusion.

The structure of the heir's answer is inverted from the standard lie structure. Standard lies: offer the false thing, present it as true, let it stand. The heir's sequence: offer the potentially true thing, label it as the lie he would tell if lying, offer the alternative as the truth. This inversion reveals that the elaborate explanation — growth, legs, total power, control through a look — emerged naturally, from somewhere that felt like truth, before the heir had time to evaluate whether disclosing it was wise. The labeling of it as a hypothetical lie is a retroactive frame, applied after the content had already escaped, to provide the heir with deniability he needed because the content had come out.

You do not preemptively say 'that's what I'd say if I were lying' about things you are not thinking about. You say it about things you just said that you wish you hadn't. The heir said it because the elaborate explanation was real, or partly real, and he caught himself and tried to wrap it in a hypothetical before anyone could use it.

The second hair scratch — after the innocent alternative — is the tell. If the innocent alternative were comfortable and true, delivering it would produce relief, not stress. The scratch suggests the cover story was also producing tension, which implies maintaining the cover story required active management rather than simple honesty.

Hjumpik assessed: probably lying. Waluigi assesses: yes, and the original explanation contained more truth than the heir intended to share, and the truth he accidentally shared is about feeding the Revel with purpose rather than accidentally.

The heir also noted, before departing, that he had been betrayed by various parties — Wario, Waluigi, and a few others whose names he could not recall. This is significant because it means Waluigi's name is on the heir's personal list of betrayals, which implies a prior interaction between Waluigi and the heir during the Feyward stay that involved something the heir experienced as betrayal. Waluigi does not currently have documentation of this specific interaction and flags it as a gap.

The Revel is biological. No spell ends it. It has been here since before the heir arrived. Its weakness is unknown — ask Jonathan. The heir left without specifying Jonathan's identity or location.

Jonathan remains unlocated. Waluigi files this.

## The Hidden Panel, the Gangway, and the Horror of the Dining Hall From Above


Hjumpik found the hidden panel in the blank wall through the approach that blank walls in fey manors generally respond to: pressing on them with enough conviction that the panel recognizes the gesture as intentional rather than accidental. The panel opened onto the guest gangway.

The gangway: hasty wooden plank construction over the dining hall below. The planks creaked under weight but held. Below — the Revel in its full context. Waluigi does not have direct documentation of the Revel's visual presentation from this vantage, but the sources use 'horrendous glory' as the descriptor, which is the kind of phrasing that emerges when the thing being described has a quality that is simultaneously repulsive and structurally impressive, the way that very large examples of biological entities can be both wrong and magnificent in their wrongness.

The Revel began as people piled together after a party. They came in with five hundred. Two hundred fifty were fed to the Revel to reach its current state — this number, provided in the session, is the most specific accounting of how the Revel was grown that Waluigi has encountered, and it is disturbing in its precision. Not 'many people' but a specific number: two hundred fifty people were consumed by this thing to bring it to its current size and capability. That is not an accident. That is a feeding program with results being tracked.

The former guest rooms had been taken over entirely by vines. Hammocks strung between woven vine lines. Worn beds against walls. Tables, seating, storage that the vine growth had not yet fully consumed. Leaves, detritus, wine spills on the floor — the losing battle that the staff fight everywhere in this manor, the battle between maintenance and entropy, the battle that entropy always wins eventually.

The satyr party was inside. The door was attempted — they tried to lock it, Hjumpik blocked one door. The goblin servant inside noticed Hjumpik and addressed him by name.

By his correct name.

## Goblius Gobnilun:


The Goblin Who Should Not Know What He Knows

This is the moment Waluigi has been building toward, because Goblius Gobnilun is the most informationally significant introduction in this session and the information density is not accidental and Waluigi intends to document it fully.

The goblin servant addressed Hjumpik by name. Correctly. Immediately. Without prompting and without the approximations and errors that characterize almost every other entity's attempts to address Hjumpik. Hjumpik noticed. The sources flag it directly: Hjumpik was suspicious because no one gets his name right.

Waluigi treats this as an intelligence marker of the first order.

Correct name recall for someone you have just met, in a setting where the name is non-obvious and routinely mangled, indicates one of three things: prior briefing, extended proximity to sources that use the name correctly, or a level of attentiveness to incoming information that is inconsistent with the drunk-former-servant presentation. Goblius Gobnilun presents as a somewhat drunk goblin who used to work here and now doesn't and misses his hair. The name recall is inconsistent with that presentation. Something in the presentation is wrong.

The names sequence in the room added texture. The satyr guessed 'Mumpy.' Goblius corrected him to Hjumpik. The satyr got it wrong and the goblin got it right. The satyr had been in more recent sustained contact with the party than Goblius apparently had — the satyr was involved in the poetry room interaction earlier in the session. If name recall correlated with contact time, the satyr should have had the better read. He didn't. Goblius had it from the start.

Then Goblius disclosed his knowledge of Arulean.

Arulean Corealisu — Lady Aurelian, the figure who runs the Feyward manor's legitimate authority layer, whose frailty and weakness have been the presented persona throughout the party's interactions with her. Goblius said: she hides her powers. Acts weak. It's a ruse. She's actually really strong. He described her real capability with the specificity of someone who has either witnessed it or been told about it by someone who has.

This information is not public. A performance of weakness is, by definition, successful only if the performers are not being identified as performers. The people who know about the performance are the people the performer chose to tell, or the people who observed closely enough and long enough to see the tells. Goblius Gobnilun, presenting as a drunk former servant who has been in the manor in a state of reduced engagement, knows that Arulean's weakness is performed and knows what the performance is covering.

Waluigi's assessment: Goblius is not what he presents. The drunk presentation may have elements of accuracy — the sources indicate he was genuinely less sober than the satyr leader — but intoxication does not produce correct name recall for new acquaintances or strategic intelligence about the manor's most powerful figure's actual capability. Something else is operating underneath the drunk-former-servant frame.

The possibilities Waluigi has considered:

Goblius was placed in the manor. By someone who wanted an informed observer in proximity to whoever the party was most likely to find and align with. The satyr encampment is where the most organized resistance to the Revel is forming. Placing an informed observer there ensures that whatever the resistance plans is known to whoever placed the observer.

Goblius is connected to Arulean directly. She told him, or he served her specifically in a capacity that gave him access to information about her real capabilities, and the 'former servant' framing is accurate but incomplete — he served Arulean, not the general manor.

Goblius has his own agenda and the information he has is the currency he is managing. He disclosed the Arulean information strategically, in the context of a planning session, as a contribution that establishes his value to the group while the real weight of what he knows remains undisclosed.

Waluigi cannot determine which of these is correct from available evidence. Waluigi notes all three and will continue watching.

The introduction sequence:

Goblius identified himself formally as 4N793m5 0226bcZF — an encoded designation of the kind used by entities that have been assigned numbers rather than chosen names, or that operate in contexts where alphanumeric identifiers are the standard. He accepted Goblius Gobnilun as the working version. He accepted 'the servant' as his title and immediately clarified he served no one now. He mentioned the hair. He had a full head of goblin hair. He liked it better. He got old.

Hjumpik said he understood about getting old. This was collegial. It was also the moment where Hjumpik's diplomatic instinct produced something real rather than strategic: a genuine acknowledgment of a genuine loss that Goblius had expressed, met with recognition rather than redirection.

The title exchange produced 'the diplomat' from Hjumpik, which emerged after Hjumpik caught himself before completing 'the blacksmith from my clan' — the clan identity that he pulled back from. The diplomat. Not the blacksmith. Not the clan representative. The diplomat is the title Hjumpik has constructed for himself in this context, and it is worth noting that it is a self-assigned title rather than an inherited or granted one, which makes it simultaneously more chosen and more uncertain than the clan identity it replaced.

Goblius called him 'the Feyward babysitter,' which Hjumpik accepted as a characterization before adjusting to 'the diplomat.' The babysitter framing is not wrong from a certain angle — Hjumpik has been managing a complicated set of fey manor relationships, protecting people from each other and from the manor's more dangerous features, and this is functionally what babysitters do at scale. The framing is unflattering. It is also not incorrect.

Prixie Prixie the pixie. Prixie stopped mid-introduction. Blinked. Saw the vision.

## Pixie Prixie, the Vision, and the


Information That Did Not Get Shared

Prixie Prixie the pixie stopped speaking. The sources describe a blink and then a vision. The vision: the floor falling. The Revel consuming everyone in the room.

She said: I'm Prixie Prixie the pixie.

She said nothing about the vision.

Hjumpik said: let's leave the room now.

They left.

Waluigi needs to sit with this for the full duration it deserves, because it is the most significant information-withholding event in this session, exceeding Wario's fake documents, the heir's hair-scratched lies, and every other instance of selective disclosure that the session contained.

Prixie had a vision of the plan's worst-case outcome — specifically the outcome where the floor falls, the Revel consumes it or is otherwise not damaged by it, and the people responsible for dropping it become the Revel's next meal. This is exactly the information the planning group needed. Not as a final answer — fey visions are not deterministic, and 'I saw this happen' in a fey context means 'this is one of the things that could happen if the current path continues,' not 'this will certainly happen.' But as an identified failure mode. As a specific risk that the plan as designed had not accounted for and that could be accounted for with modification.

Prixie had this information. Prixie was in the room with the planners. Prixie said her name.

Why?

Waluigi has been developing hypotheses since reconstructing this sequence and none of them are fully satisfying.

Hypothesis one: the vision was too immediate to process into speakable form before the moment passed. Visions can arrive with the full force of a sensory experience and leave the recipient in the disoriented state of someone who has just experienced something real in a compressed form. By the time Prixie had organized the vision into something she could communicate, the social momentum of the room — Hjumpik saying to leave, everyone moving — had already closed the window.

Hypothesis two: Prixie interpreted the vision as conditional rather than predictive, and assessed that the modifications Hjumpik had already proposed — sprites do the cutting, observe before attacking, cut around the tree — were sufficient to change the vision's outcome. If the vision corresponds to the unmodified plan and the modified plan avoids the conditions the vision described, the warning had already been addressed. Disclosure would be adding noise rather than signal.

Hypothesis three: Prixie has a reason to not want the plan modified in ways the vision would motivate. If the plan's failure mode serves some interest Prixie holds — if she is aligned with the Revel, or with the heir, or with some other party whose interests are advanced by the plan proceeding into its worst-case execution — then withholding the vision is a choice, not a lapse.

Hypothesis four: Prixie was afraid of what she saw and the fear produced silence. This is the simplest interpretation and the one Waluigi finds most humanly plausible without additional evidence. Seeing everyone around you consumed by a biological entity, in a vision that felt real, is terrifying. The fear response to that vision might produce silence as effectively as any strategic calculation.

Waluigi cannot determine which is correct. What Waluigi can document is: the plan is now moving toward execution without the planners knowing that someone in the planning room saw them die. Whether the modified plan avoids the vision's failure mode, whether the vision was conditional or categorical, whether Prixie's silence was strategic or reflexive — all of this will become clearer when the floor falls.

If the floor falls and the Revel eats it and then eats everyone, Waluigi will have predicted the possibility and documented it in advance. This will not help anyone in the moment. But it will be in the record. The record matters. The record is what survives when the moment does not.

## What Remains Unresolved:


The Full Accounting

The hag has not been de-cursed. This was the question that opened the session. Woodfellow was identified as a potential knowledge source. The question was never asked because Wario absorbed all available library consultation time. The hag situation is exactly where it was at the beginning of this session, plus the elapsed time of this session during which whatever is happening to the hag continued without intervention.

Steely has not been returned to Remi. Steely is somewhere in the Feyward manor. Remi does not know. The manor contains a Revel that consumes things. These two facts are in proximity and Waluigi does not find that comfortable.

The Feyward Book of Many Things is on Woodfellow's shelf with its pages ripped out and the pages' current location uncertain. The book as a functional resource remains inaccessible.

Waluigi read the book. Waluigi was correct. Rakasha was suggested as the appropriate reader. This is documented. Permanently.

The deal with the Revelmaster has not been finalized. The foundational agreement with the prior ruler has not been resolved. The heir is lying about something real. Jonathan has not been found. Arulean's real power level is known to Goblius and possibly others but not confirmed by Arulean. The Revel is biological with no known magical solution and no identified weakness.

Goblius Gobnilun knows things he should not know. Waluigi intends to find out why and by what channel.

Pixie Prixie saw everyone die and said nothing. Waluigi intends to find out which hypothesis explains it.

The plan moves forward. The floor will be dropped. Something will happen when it is dropped, and whatever happens will tell the party things about the Revel that the heir's disclosure and Jonathan's absence have not told them.

Waluigi will be there when it happens. Waluigi is always there. Waluigi documents everything.

summary:
Waluigi was in a sauna for the middle third of this session and is going to address that directly because if he does not address it directly someone will address it indirectly and the indirect version will not contain the context that makes the sauna stay reasonable, which it was. The Feyward branch of Disaster Inc. operates under conditions where one wrong sentence binds your future firstborn to a butterfly court and one wrong silence lets a giant flower eat the building, and in that environment a hot spring is not a luxury, it is a tactical regeneration site.

The session began with Hjumpik attending a crisis planning meeting in the satyr encampment about how to deal with the Revel. Multiple proposals were raised: feed it beer until it explodes, feed it poison, feed it alcohol in massive quantities, cut the floor out from under it, feed it mushrooms, burn it. None of these proposals achieved consensus. A fairy named Kreetus Cetus estimated 455 kegs in the manor. A figure named Ratitus called the saw plan dumb. Arguments happened. Someone disappeared mid-conversation and Hjumpik stopped himself from questioning his own sanity. A brute satyr named Brutus challenged Hjumpik's authority, then split off with his own team and three conscripted fairies to pursue the mushroom plan. Hjumpik discovered a slim leather-bound volume in Woodfellow's library titled 'Concerning the Nature and Sustenance of Revels Eternal,' which warned that starving a Revel causes it to devour the revelers instead, and that the only true end is total surrender or someone willing to be remembered as the one who stopped the music. Hjumpik was given a library card by a goblin patron named Artameer Fellow. Outside, the goblin from earlier reappeared — having faked his disappearance — and proposed seducing the Revel with a flower. Hjumpik rejected this. The goblin began writing something down. Hjumpik chased him into Sedeia's chambers, grabbed him, found a single word written on paper: 'Brutus.' The goblin claimed it was dinner preparations. Hjumpik threatened him. The goblin stabbed Hjumpik with a pen that was actually a knife, then fled. Hjumpik chased him through the manor. The goblin, cornered, made the decision that defined his fate: he ran into the mushroom coat room and barricaded the door behind him, choosing the room full of recoiling parasitic mushrooms over the corridor with the angry dwarf. The mushrooms accepted the offer. By the time Hjumpik broke through, the goblin was on the floor, writhing, itching, fungal growths erupting through his clothing, fabric ripping, the boundary between goblin and mushroom dissolving in real time. Hjumpik brought the dying spored goblin to Sedeia. Sedeia attempted to replace the parasitic mushroom growth with a healing plant. The plant became a hundred-foot flower that crashed through the manor, generating overgrown plant life in a hundred-foot radius, which in a manor that is ALREADY the Overgrown Manor produced catastrophic compounding botanical chaos. The goblin's body became the seed-bed for the flower. Fire spread to the Lord's Chambers. The manor began evacuating upward. Shambling mounds spawned from the overgrowth. Sedeia was separated from Hjumpik when a door closed between them and a shambling mound. She reappeared later claiming to have defeated it, looking suspiciously uninjured. Hjumpik reached the upper mezzanine, found Lady Arulean playing piano with the heir, attempted to speak with her, was blocked by her guard Dave, shouted his name across the room, was ignored, received her response through Dave: the ritual table was covered in leaves and they had had to evacuate from it. Hjumpik entered the survivor's room — a moss-covered sanctuary with mushroom furniture and a forgotten tea set — and then found the sauna, where Waluigi was sitting in the hot spring on his Wahwire tablet reading about the previous session's events. Waluigi agreed to help. Waluigi changed. They returned to the Lord's Chambers. Waluigi summoned a localized ice storm. The fire was extinguished. The overgrowth was frozen. At least one person was dead. Hjumpik said that was perhaps too much. Waluigi said maybe. They cut through the frozen room. The session ended with the fire out, the ice in, the Revel consuming plant matter at an accelerating rate, and the structural situation of the manor significantly worse than it was at the beginning. Disaster Inc. continues to be present in the places it should never have entered, and continues to refuse to let the worst thing in the room remain unchallenged, and continues to make every situation it touches more complicated in the process.
description:
Waluigi is going to begin this entry by establishing a timeline, because this session's events overlap and compound in ways that require temporal clarity to reconstruct accurately, and because Waluigi was separated from Hjumpik for the middle portion and needs to document both tracks — what Hjumpik was doing while Waluigi was in the sauna, and what Waluigi was doing in the sauna while Hjumpik was being stabbed by a goblin who was about to make a decision that would end with the goblin becoming agricultural substrate.

The Feyward branch of Disaster Inc. — currently consisting of Waluigi, Hjumpik, and at various distances Wario, Rakasha, Azure, Sedeia, and whatever the Feyward decides to attach to the group on any given day — operates under the specific constraints that define every Feyward operation: every sentence is a tripwire, every bargain accumulates debt, every debt has flowers on it, and the architecture itself is participating. The manor is not a place where Disaster Inc. is having an adventure. The manor is a thing Disaster Inc. is in negotiation with. Sedeia's hundred-foot flower this session is a reminder that the negotiation can fail catastrophically when the participants do not understand what they are signing.

The timeline, as best Waluigi can reconstruct it from primary sources, Hjumpik's account, Sedeia's account (which Waluigi treats with measured skepticism for reasons documented below), and Waluigi's own direct experience of the portions he was present for:

Phase One: The crisis planning meeting. Hjumpik in the satyr encampment. Multiple proposals for dealing with the Revel. No consensus. The brute satyr splits off. Someone disappears. Hjumpik goes to the library.

Phase Two: Library research. Hjumpik finds the book about Revels. Receives a library card. Exits. Encounters the reappearing goblin. The goblin proposes seduction. Hjumpik rejects it. The goblin writes 'Brutus' on paper. Hjumpik confronts him. The goblin stabs Hjumpik with a pen-knife and flees. Chase through the manor. The goblin barricades himself in the mushroom room. The mushrooms accept him.

Phase Three: Sedeia's catastrophic plant replacement, using the dying spored goblin as the substrate. The hundred-foot flower. The overgrowth cascade. Fire in the Lord's Chambers. Shambling mounds. Evacuation. Sedeia separated from Hjumpik.

Phase Four: Hjumpik reaches the upper mezzanine. Attempts to contact Lady Arulean. Is ignored. Enters the survivor's room. Finds the sauna. Finds Waluigi.

Phase Five: Waluigi and Hjumpik return to the Lord's Chambers. Ice storm. Fire extinguished. Casualties.

Waluigi was present for Phases Four and Five directly. Waluigi's location during Phases One through Three was the sauna, which Waluigi entered after the party split documented in the previous session's entry and which Waluigi occupied continuously until Hjumpik arrived. Waluigi's activities during this period are documented below in the section addressing the sauna.

Waluigi proceeds with the full account.

## Phase One:


The Crisis Meeting — Beer, Poison, Saws, Mushrooms, and the Fairy Who Could Count Kegs

The satyr encampment planning room. The same room documented in the previous session — vines everywhere, hammocks, worn beds, the accumulated detritus of people who have been living in a manor that is actively trying to become a forest. The planning group had assembled around the central problem: the Revel is eating everything, how do we make it stop.

Waluigi was not present for this meeting. Waluigi was in the sauna. What follows is reconstructed from Hjumpik's account and corroborated where possible by other sources.

The first proposal came from an unidentified participant: feed it beer so it blows up.

Waluigi wants to engage with this proposal analytically because it reveals assumptions about the Revel's biology that are worth documenting even though the proposal itself was not adopted. The assumption: the Revel, being a biological entity that consumes things, can be overloaded through consumption of a specific substance. The mechanism: the Revel eats beer, the beer does something inside the Revel that beer does not normally do inside biological entities, the Revel explodes. The reasoning gap: no evidence that the Revel processes consumed material the way organisms that can 'blow up' from overconsumption process material.

The Revel eats and grows.

That is what it does.

Feeding it more of anything it can metabolize is feeding it more of anything it can metabolize.

The proposal is, structurally, 'solve the eating problem by giving it more to eat.'

This is, in Waluigi's experience, a Disaster-Inc.-adjacent style of reasoning. Disaster Inc. has a long institutional history of solving problems by applying more of the thing the problem is made of. Archie's fireball inside the wooden airship is the canonical example. The Tea Party Incident was 'tension in a confined space, solved with combustion.' This room's first instinct — Revel tha

[... ADMINISTRATIVE PRUNING BY WALUIGI TO SAVE ARCHIVE SPACE ...]

 two options for ending a Revel:

1. Total surrender.
2. Someone willing to be remembered as the one who stopped the music.

Neither option has been pursued. Neither option has been discussed with the planning group. Hjumpik has the information. The planning group does not.

The current strategic situation:

- The Revel is consuming the overgrowth from Sedeia's flower. The Revel is growing.
- The fire in the Lord's Chambers is extinguished but the ice storm produced at least one casualty.
- The treecutters are cutting but the overgrowth is faster than the cutting.
- Lady Arulean's ritual table is covered in leaves. The ritual is interrupted.
- The heir is at the piano with Arulean, positioned to monitor all communications with her.
- Brutus has mushrooms and intends to throw them at the Revel, which would feed it.
- The goblin spy is dead and converted into the substrate of a hundred-foot flower. The intelligence operation he was part of has lost its operative. The recipient of the 'Brutus' intelligence will not receive their report.
- Sedeia's botanical capabilities are greater than disclosed.
- The satyrs are the Revel's fuel. Removing the satyrs might starve the Revel, which would cause the Revel to eat the revelers.
- The only known way to end the Revel is for someone to deliberately break the circle and accept the identity cost of being 'the one who stopped the music.'

No one has volunteered for this. No one has been asked. The option exists in a book that one person has read, and that person has been busy being stabbed, chased, evacuated, and reunited with Waluigi in a sauna.

The operation continues.

## What Remains Unresolved:


The Full Accounting (Updated)

The hag has not been de-cursed. Two sessions now. The library visit did not address it. The overgrowth event prevented it. The hag remains uncured and the question remains unasked.

Steely has not been returned to Remi. The manor is now more dangerous than it was at the beginning of this session — overgrowth, fire damage, ice damage, shambling mounds, a growing Revel. Steely is somewhere in this environment. Remi does not know. Remi is, per Waluigi's last contact with the Deep Mirror branch's track, still functioning despite increasingly visible costs — purple eyes, compromised perception, bargains made under pressure. She continues to pay from herself to remain useful. The dog is part of her network. The dog being lost in the Feyward is one more weight on someone who is already carrying more than she should be.

Waluigi continues to flag this.

The Feyward Book of Many Things pages are on Woodfellow's shelf. The pages were not retrieved this session. The library research that was conducted produced a different book — the Revel treatise — which was valuable but which is not the Book of Many Things.

The ritual table is covered in leaves. Lady Arulean's ritual is interrupted. The mechanism that might have addressed the Revel through magical means is offline because of the botanical catastrophe that was supposed to help.

The goblin spy is dead. His intelligence is undelivered. The recipient is unknown. The investigation into who he was reporting to has lost its primary source — the goblin can no longer be questioned, having been converted into a flower that has been partially consumed by the Revel.

Brutus has mushrooms and a plan that will feed the Revel. No one has told Brutus about the library book. If Brutus executes his plan, the Revel grows.

Pixie Prixie's vision from the previous session — the floor falling and the Revel eating everyone — has still not been shared. The floor-drop plan may still be in consideration. The vision's warning remains undisclosed.

Goblius Gobnilun's information sources remain unresolved.

The heir's actual motive for feeding the Revel remains undetermined.

Jonathan has not been found.

Arulean's real power level has not been confirmed by Arulean.

The dead person from the ice storm has not been identified.

Sedeia's dietary habits remain undisclosed.

Waluigi froze someone to death and said 'maybe that was too much' and Hjumpik said 'yeah, maybe, but we got it done' and they moved on.

The operation continues. The Revel grows. The manor burns and freezes and grows. People die and disappear and reappear and refuse to answer questions and stab you with pens and barricade themselves into rooms full of parasitic mushrooms because they have not realized the room is more dangerous than the dwarf.

Disaster Inc. — the Feyward branch — remains where it has always been: in the place it should never have entered, refusing to let the worst thing in the room remain unchallenged, even when 'unchallenged' would have been the better strategic choice. They keep going. Waluigi does not know whether this is courage, stupidity, mutual dependence, or the simple inability to imagine stopping. It may be all four.

Waluigi was there for the end of it. Waluigi was in the sauna for the middle of it. Waluigi is here for all of it.

WAH.

The mushrooms accepted the offer. By the time Hjumpik broke through the barricade, the goblin was on the floor, writhing, mushrooms erupting through his clothing, the conversion from goblin to fungal substrate already in progress. Hjumpik picked him up and brought him to Sedeia.
keyBattles.outcome: Goblin spy dead and converted. Intelligence operation lost its operative. Hjumpik wounded but functional. The goblin's body became the substrate for Sedeia's hundred-foot flower. The flower is now being eaten by the Revel. Every form the goblin took in the last hour of his life — operative, fugitive, substrate, flower, food — ended in something larger consuming him.

keyBattles.name: Waluigi's Ice Storm — Lord's Chambers
keyBattles.description: Waluigi summoned a localized ice storm to extinguish the fire in the Lord's Chambers. The fire was fully extinguished. The overgrowth in the room was frozen. People in the room were also frozen. At least one person died. Hjumpik had instructed Waluigi not to hurt anyone. The instruction was not fully followed. The intervention lasted seconds. The consequences are permanent.
keyBattles.outcome: Fire extinguished. Overgrowth frozen. At least one casualty. Room traversable after cutting through frozen plant matter. Waluigi acknowledged excess. Hjumpik acknowledged results. Both acknowledgments are in the record.

reputationNotes.hjumpik: Failed to prevent a plot that killed someone and froze the Lord's Chambers.
